channel.title: Cadence 步频 — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 50 sources.

item.title: FY 2027 Inpatient Rehabilitation Facilities (IRF) Prospective Payment System (PPS) Final Rule (CMS-1845-F)
item.description: CMS has issued the Fiscal Year 2027 Inpatient Rehabilitation Facilities (IRF) Prospective Payment System (PPS) Final Rule.
item.author: CMS

item.title: Structured exercise training for fatigue management in multiple sclerosis: an umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses.
item.description: An umbrella review synthesizing evidence from systematic reviews and meta-analyses confirms the effectiveness of structured exercise training for fatigue in people with multiple sclerosis, with effects varying across exercise modalities and fatigue instruments.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Clinical practice guideline for physical therapist management of total knee arthroplasty: revision 2026.
item.description: An American Physical Therapy Association volunteer group has updated the clinical practice guideline for total knee arthroplasty, formulating 20 recommendations based on a systematic review of current literature.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effectiveness of an AI-based home exercise app for rehabilitation of rotator cuff-related shoulder pain: A randomized controlled trial.
item.description: A single-center RCT (N=46) found that adding an AI-based digital rehabilitation program to standard physiotherapy significantly improved pain, function, and fear-avoidance beliefs, and reduced healthcare utilization in patients with rotator cuff-related shoulder pain.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Remotely Monitored Home-based Pulmonary Rehabilitation in Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis: Results of a Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (N=29) in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis on antifibrotic therapy found that a 12-week asynchronously remotely monitored, exercise-focused home pulmonary rehabilitation program significantly improved exercise capacity (increase in 6MWD by 31.6 meters; p=0.03).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Skilled Nursing Facility PPS
item.description: CMS issued the FY 2027 Skilled Nursing Facility Prospective Payment System proposed rule, outlining updates to Medicare payment policies and rates, with comments due by June 1.
item.author: CMS

item.title: Hydrodilatation for adhesive capsulitis: a systematic review exploring efficacy and optimal technique.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 103 studies (9951 patients, 44 RCTs) explored the efficacy and optimal technique of hydrodilatation for adhesive capsulitis. The median hydrodilatation volume across studies was 28 mL (range: 8.3-200 mL).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Beyond "Biomedical-Plus": Reclaiming the biopsychosocial model in musculoskeletal physiotherapy.
item.description: This commentary argues that musculoskeletal physiotherapy often implements the biopsychosocial (BPS) model as "biomedical-plus" care. It proposes that physiotherapists can achieve a more authentic BPS application through three foundational conditions: professional Confidence, role Clarity, and Compassionate communication.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: 河南省人民政府办公厅关于印发河南省建立长期护理保险制度实施方案的通知-健康界
item.description: Henan Province, China, issued an implementation plan for establishing a long-term care insurance system, aiming to fully establish the system across the province within about three years to cover employees, retirees, flexible workers, and unemployed urban and rural residents.
item.author: 健康界

item.title: Content validity, reliability, and agreement between in-person and video-call assessments of the modified bradykinesia rating scale (MBRS).
item.description: The Modified Bradykinesia Rating Scale (MBRS) showed adequate content validity, good test-retest reliability (ICC=0.98), inter-rater reliability (ICC=0.97), and agreement between in-person and video-call assessments (ICC=0.97) for assessing bradykinesia in individuals with Parkinson's disease.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: In adult patients with brainstem strokes, does dysphagia rehabilitation improve health-related outcomes compared to usual care for inpatients? A systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 12 studies (443 participants) suggests that dysphagia rehabilitation is effective in improving swallow function in inpatients with brainstem stroke, with interventions categorized into traditional swallowing therapy or inclusion of devices.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: A systematic review of current evidence on clinical outcomes of lumbar roll and modified SIMS manipulation techniques in sacroiliac joint dysfunction.
item.description: This appears to be a protocol for a systematic review of lumbar roll and modified SIMS manipulation techniques for sacroiliac joint dysfunction, registered on PROSPERO with a search period through 2025.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Exploring equity in telehealth interventions in physiotherapy: A meta-epidemiological study.
item.description: This meta-epidemiological study assessed equity in telehealth physiotherapy interventions using the PROGRESS Plus framework, analyzing 94 randomized controlled trials from 2020-2023 to understand how telehealth addresses or exacerbates health disparities.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Responsiveness of the Arabic version of the lower extremity functional scale in individuals with lower extremity musculoskeletal disorders.
item.description: The Arabic version of the Lower Extremity Functional Scale (LEFS) showed good responsiveness in 74 participants with lower extremity musculoskeletal disorders, with LEFS change scores correlating well with changes in other outcome measures.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Research progress on horticultural therapy in patients with post-stroke cognitive impairment: a narrative review.
item.description: A narrative review suggests horticultural therapy significantly improves memory, executive function, and orientation in post-stroke cognitive impairment patients, also benefiting mood and ADL, via sequential and repetitive cognitive demands.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: The Association of Depression, Anxiety, and Quality of Life with Sexual Function in Young-to-Middle-Aged Stroke Patients: A Case-Control Study.
item.description: A case-control study of young-to-middle-aged stroke patients (n=30) found significantly higher rates of sexual dysfunction compared to controls (19.3 ± 6.6 vs. 13.0 ± 3.1, p < 0.001), associated with depression, anxiety, and poorer quality of life.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Information and communication technologies in implementation strategies promoting allied health professionals' guideline adherence in post-acute stroke care: a scoping review.
item.description: A scoping review mapped the use of information and communication technologies (ICTs) in implementation strategies to promote allied health professionals' guideline adherence in post-acute stroke care, categorizing ICTs based on targeted determinants of practice.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Correlation of Motor-Task Related Brain Activation Changes With Motor Performance Changes Induced by Constraint-Induced Therapy After Stroke.
item.description: An fMRI study in 42 hemiparetic stroke patients undergoing Constraint-Induced Movement Therapy (CIMT) found changes in motor-task related brain activation correlated with improvements in functional recovery assessed by the Wolf Motor Function Test.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Multimodal Phenotyping of Myofascial Pain Syndrome Using Rotational Shear Wave Elastography and Clinical Network Analysis
item.description: A study explored multimodal phenotyping of myofascial pain syndrome (MPS) using rotational shear wave elastography (SWE), bioimpedance spectroscopy (BIS), range of motion (ROM), and patient-reported outcomes (PROs) in 71 adults, aiming to objectively characterize MPS subgroups.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Models Containing the Braden Scale Predict Activities of Daily Living Improvement in Post-Stroke Hemiplegia: A Single Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
item.description: A single-center retrospective cohort study on 324 post-stroke hemiplegia patients developed a predictive model integrating the Braden scale to forecast activities of daily living (ADL) recovery and evaluated a comprehensive rehabilitation program.
item.author: PubMed
